methods.name: Speaking goals aloud (production effect, self-explanation)
methods.userDoes: Answers the interview and confirms each goal by saying it
methods.why: Words spoken aloud are remembered better than words read silently; explaining a goal in your own words exposes vague ones
methods.confidenceDetail: Strong for memory; moderate for goal pursuit
methods.source: MacLeod et al. 2010; Chi et al. 1989; Bisra et al. 2018 meta-analysis

methods.name: Writing goals down and reporting progress
methods.userDoes: Hierarchy is saved in the user's words; weekly outcomes recorded
methods.why: Written, specific goals with progress reports outperformed unwritten goals in a 4-week study; the effect is commitment and accountability more than the ink
methods.confidenceDetail: Matthews 2015: n=267, self-report, four weeks, not a large replicated trial. The "Harvard 3% study" is a myth
methods.source: Matthews 2015 (Dominican University); Locke & Latham 2002 for goal specificity (strong)

methods.name: Proximal subgoals (goal hierarchy)
methods.userDoes: Every goal has a parent; weekly priorities thread to monthly goals
methods.why: Near-term subgoals tied to a distal goal raise persistence and self-efficacy more than distal goals alone

methods.name: Self-concordant goals (want vs should)
methods.userDoes: Answers "desire or should?" and "does saying it energize or drain you?"
methods.why: Goals pursued for autonomous reasons get sustained effort and better attainment than goals pursued from pressure

methods.name: Implementation intentions
methods.userDoes: States an if-then plan for each weekly priority and each next action
methods.why: Pre-deciding when, where and how an action happens makes the cue trigger it; d ≈ 0.65 across 94 studies

methods.name: Mental contrasting with implementation intentions (WOOP)
methods.userDoes: Names the wish, imagines the outcome, names the obstacle, plans the step
methods.why: Contrasting the wish with the obstacle converts fantasy into effort; positive fantasy alone lowers energy
methods.confidenceDetail: Strong for MCII (g ≈ 0.34); strong for the fantasy warning
methods.source: Oettingen 2012; Kappes & Oettingen 2011; Wang et al. 2021 meta-analysis

methods.name: Process vs outcome simulation
methods.userDoes: Walks through the first two minutes of today's step rather than the finished result
methods.why: Rehearsing the process raised studying and grades; rehearsing the outcome did not

methods.name: Retrieval practice and spacing
methods.userDoes: Hears one life goal and one 5-year goal each morning on a rotating schedule and says the thread back
methods.why: Recalling an item strengthens it more than re-reading it; spacing the recalls beats massing them
methods.confidenceDetail: Strong for memory; moderate for keeping goals salient
methods.source: Roediger & Karpicke 2006; Cepeda et al. 2006; Dunlosky et al. 2013

methods.name: Distanced self-talk
methods.userDoes: Reframes a negative thought in the third person or by name
methods.why: Addressing yourself by name regulates emotion without extra cognitive effort
methods.source: Kross et al. 2014; Moser et al. 2017; Orvell et al. 2021

methods.name: Cognitive restructuring (labeling distortions)
methods.userDoes: Hears the distortion named and offers a believable alternative
methods.why: Core CBT technique; identifying the distortion weakens its automaticity

methods.name: Self-compassion after setbacks
methods.userDoes: Closes a missed priority with one neutral sentence and a correction
methods.why: Self-compassion after failure increases motivation to improve and persistence; self-criticism reduces both
methods.source: Breines & Chen 2012; Neff 2003; Ferrari et al. 2019 meta-analysis

methods.name: Self-affirmation (values)
methods.userDoes: End-of-life scene and the monthly "why this goal matters to who I am"
methods.why: Writing about core values buffers identity threat and improves follow-through in some settings; large-scale replications are mixed

methods.name: Own-voice playback
methods.userDoes: Records three scenes and hears them in Morning Course
methods.why: Hearing your own voice state a goal is rated more believable than a stranger's; a self-reference effect is plausible
methods.confidenceDetail: Review evidence (ThinkUp, Stella) and self-reference memory effects, no direct trial

methods.name: Mental rehearsal and "cells that fire together wire together"
methods.userDoes: Rehearses the step as the person who already does it
methods.why: Mental practice improves later performance, mostly on cognitive tasks, and is weaker than physical practice; the Hebbian line is a popular framing of synaptic plasticity, not a goal-pursuit finding. Dispenza's broader claims (elevated emotion changing biology) are not established
methods.confidenceDetail: Emerging / mixed. Moderate for mental practice itself
methods.source: Hebb 1949; Pascual-Leone et al. 1995; Driskell et al. 1994 meta-analysis; concept §5

notes.note: Answer out loud. Spoken answers are remembered better and expose vague goals.
Describe a concrete day, not a result. Concrete scenes become plans; vague wishes do not.
This names what matters to you. Stating core values helps you hold to them under pressure.
Each goal is saved in your words and tied to your own sentence. Written, specific goals are acted on more.
Every goal needs a parent. Near goals tied to far goals keep you going longer.

notes.moment: Interview: want vs should, body check
notes.note: Goals you want outlast goals you should. Say it; if it drains you, rewrite it.
Add when and where. If-then plans roughly double follow-through.
Record it yourself. People rate goals in their own voice as more believable.
Say the thread back. Recalling a goal keeps it active; re-reading does not.
Picture the first two minutes, not the finish. Process rehearsal raises follow-through.
Name the obstacle, then the plan. Wish plus obstacle plus plan beats wishing alone.
Use your name. Talking to yourself by name lowers the heat without extra effort.

notes.moment: Morning Course: correction after a miss
notes.note: A miss gets a step, not a verdict. Self-compassion after failure raises persistence.
Say the problem out loud. Explaining it exposes the real question.
Every talk ends in one step with a time. Decided steps get done.
One sentence per priority, no guilt. Neutral review keeps you in the game.
Three priorities, each tied to a monthly goal. Subgoals with a parent get done.
Say when and where. If-then plans roughly double follow-through.
Rewrite or drop stale goals. Letting go of unreachable goals and re-engaging protects effort and wellbeing.
Rehearse, then plan. Picturing the result alone lowers effort; always end with the obstacle and the step.
notes.confidenceDetail: Strong for the warning; emerging for rehearsal
